title: How do you draw a square when you know only its diagonal?
description: Only the diagonal of a square is known, eight centimetres. The video draws the diagonal, its midpoint and a line at right angles to it, and Keeko then doubts and takes the eight centimetres to be a side.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a square are equal, cut each other in half and cross at ninety degrees, so drawing them first gives the square. Watch for students who build the square on a side of the given length.

source: Construct a square with a diagonal of 8 cm.
video_script.why: The child draws a square from its diagonal alone, using the facts that its diagonals are equal, cut each other in half and cross at right angles.
video_script.substitution: Draw the diagonal, mark its midpoint, draw a line at right angles through the midpoint, mark the other two corners at the same distance, and join the four corners.
video_script.anchor: diagonal AC of 8 cm with midpoint O and a line at right angles through O
video_script.wrong_answer: the eight centimetres is the side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the eight centimetres to be a side and builds the square on it; but then the diagonal comes out longer than eight centimetres, so the eight centimetres belongs to the diagonal.
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh B C D is the square, with both diagonals eight centimetres

final_answer.value: ABCD is the square, with diagonals AC = BD = 8 cm
final_answer.spoken: eigh B C D is the square, with both diagonals eight centimetres

maths_rules: the diagonals of a square are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90 degrees
AC = 8 cm and O is its midpoint, so OA = OC = 4 cm
BD is perpendicular to AC at O with OB = OD = 4 cm, so BD = 8 cm = AC
equal diagonals that bisect each other at 90 degrees make a square
a square with a side of 8 cm has a diagonal longer than 8 cm, so 8 cm cannot be the side
video_script.design: One idea: draw the diagonals first, equal and crossing at right angles at their midpoints. Wrong idea: the given eight centimetres is a side. The diagonal AC with its midpoint stays on the board.
